paragraphs: Words from Our Emails, posted by May. I write the emails to our pen pals. Last week, Teacher Kim asked us to find word parts in the mail that we send and receive. She says that this is a good way to learn vocabulary. We keep a vocabulary notebook, and I write every new word in it. It is a fun game, and every Explorer can play it.

The prefix "un" means "not". One email from Grace was unread for two days, because I did not click on it. Another email had an unclear word. I did not know the word, so I asked Teacher Kim. She was very helpful, and she showed me the answer in a dictionary. Now I click on every new email at once.

The prefix "re" means "again". Leo's photo did not go to Ravi, so he had to resend it. Then Leo clicked "resend", and the photo went at once. I always reread my email before I click "send". Then I make the message better, and I send it. Mia says that this is a good habit.

The suffix "er" can mean "a person who does something". The sender is the person who sends the email. The reader is the person who opens it. I am a writer, because I write the emails for the Explorers. Teacher Kim is the first reader of every post, and she is also our teacher. The same suffix can give us many new words.

The suffix "less" means "without", and the suffix "ful" means "full of". A careless child tells a friend the password for an email account. A short password is useless, because other people can find it. A helpful password is long, and it has letters and numbers. Mia made a good password with a long sentence and some numbers. I suppose that Leo is right when he says, "Never share a password."

The suffix "ly" makes many adverbs, for example "slowly" and "happily". Mia likes "happily", because it sounds like a smile. At the school event, Mia took photos carefully, and Leo drew quickly. My vocabulary notebook now has fifty new words. I wrote about the event in an email, and Grace answered with a long message. Grace asked, "How is Pip?" Which word parts do you see in your messages? Tell us in a comment!
text.summary: May writes a blog post about the word parts that the Explorers found in their emails to the pen-pal class. She gives examples with un, re, er, less, ful, and ly, and she tells about a good password.
